ko.B: 너희가 어떤 성읍을 점령하려고 오랫동안 포위하고 싸울 때에, 그 성읍의 나무들을 도끼로 찍어 없애지 말라. 너희는 그 열매를 먹을 수 있으니, 그 나무들을 베어 버리지 말라. 들의 나무가 사람이라도 되느냐? 너희가 그 나무까지 포위해야 하겠느냐?
ko.R: 여러분은 어떤 성읍을 점령하려고 오랫동안 에워싸고 싸워야 할 때가 있을 것입니다. 그럴 때에도 그곳의 과일나무들을 도끼로 찍어 없애면 안 됩니다. 그 열매를 먹을 수 있으니 베어 버리지 마십시오. 나무는 사람이 아닙니다. 여러분이 싸우는 적이 아닙니다.

decisions.choice: is the tree of the field a man, to come before you in the siege?: a question expecting "no"
alternatives: for the man [is] the tree of the field
for a man's life [is] the tree of the field
decisions.reason: The vowels of the Hebrew text read the first word as a question: trees are not enemy soldiers, that they should be besieged and destroyed with the city. Read without the question, the words say "for the man [is] the tree of the field", which has been taken to mean that human life depends on such trees. Both readings lead to the same command: the trees that feed people are to be spared.

decisions.choice: do not destroy its trees: a limit on the ruin of war
decisions.reason: Armies besieging a city often cut down its orchards, both for timber and to ruin the land for years (2 Kings 3:19, 25). Moses forbids this for fruit trees, which feed people long after the war (verse 20).

decisions.choice: swinging an ax against it
decisions.reason: The verb means to drive or swing; it is used of a man swinging an ax at a tree in 19:5.

decisions.choice: from it you may eat: permission
decisions.reason: The verb can say what Israel will do or what it may do. Here it gives permission: the besiegers may eat the fruit, but not destroy the trees.

decisions.choice: fruit trees
decisions.reason: Readable says "fruit trees", since the verse speaks of trees whose fruit is eaten and verse 20 sets other trees apart.

decisions.choice: Trees are not people. They are not the enemy you are fighting.
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects (m1) instead of asking it.

source.text: רַ֞ק עֵ֣ץ אֲשֶׁר־תֵּדַ֗ע כִּֽי־לֹא־עֵ֤ץ מַאֲכָל֙ ה֔וּא אֹת֥וֹ תַשְׁחִ֖ית וְכָרָ֑תָּ וּבָנִ֣יתָ מָצ֗וֹר עַל־הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁר־הִ֨וא עֹשָׂ֧ה עִמְּךָ֛ מִלְחָמָ֖ה עַ֥ד רִדְתָּֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Only a tree that you know that not a tree of food it [is], it you may destroy and cut down, and you shall build siege works against the city which it [is] making with you war, until its going down.

en.L: Only a tree that you know is not a tree for food, it you may destroy and cut down, and you shall build siege works against the city that is making war with you, until it falls.
en.B: Only the trees that you know do not give food may you destroy and cut down, to build siege works against the city that is at war with you, until it falls.
en.R: But you may cut down trees that you know do not give food. Use them to build ramps and towers to attack the city that is fighting you, until it is defeated.

es.L: Solo el árbol que sepas que no es árbol [que da] alimento, ese podrás destruirlo y cortarlo, y construirás obras de asedio contra la ciudad que te hace la guerra, hasta que caiga.
es.B: Solo los árboles que sepas que no dan alimento podrás destruir y cortar, para construir obras de asedio contra la ciudad que está en guerra contigo, hasta que caiga.
es.R: Pero puedes cortar los árboles que sepas que no dan alimento. Úsalos para construir rampas y torres para atacar la ciudad que pelea contra ti, hasta que sea derrotada.

fr.L: Seulement, l’arbre dont tu sauras que ce n’est pas un arbre [qui donne] de la nourriture, celui-là tu pourras le détruire et l’abattre, et tu bâtiras des ouvrages de siège contre la ville qui te fait la guerre, jusqu’à ce qu’elle tombe.
fr.B: Seuls les arbres dont tu sais qu’ils ne donnent pas de nourriture, tu pourras les détruire et les abattre, pour bâtir des ouvrages de siège contre la ville qui est en guerre contre toi, jusqu’à ce qu’elle tombe.
fr.R: Mais tu peux couper les arbres dont tu sais qu’ils ne donnent pas de nourriture. Sers-t’en pour construire des rampes et des tours pour attaquer la ville qui te combat, jusqu’à ce qu’elle soit vaincue.

sw.L: Ila mti utakaoujua kwamba si mti wa chakula, huo unaweza kuuharibu na kuukata, nawe utajenga ngome za kuzingira juu ya mji unaofanya vita nawe, hadi utakapoanguka.
sw.B: Ni miti tu unayoijua kwamba haitoi chakula unayoweza kuiharibu na kuikata, ili kujenga ngome za kuuzingira mji ulio vitani nawe, hadi utakapoanguka.
sw.R: Lakini unaweza kukata miti unayoijua kwamba haitoi chakula. Itumie kujenga vilima na minara ya kuushambulia mji unaopigana nawe, hadi utakaposhindwa.

vi.L: Chỉ có cây mà ngươi biết không phải là cây cho thức ăn, ngươi mới được phá hủy và đốn nó, và ngươi được xây công sự vây hãm chống lại thành đang gây chiến với ngươi, cho đến khi nó sụp đổ.
vi.B: Chỉ những cây anh em biết là không cho trái ăn được thì anh em mới được phá và đốn, để xây công sự vây hãm thành đang giao chiến với anh em, cho đến khi thành ấy thất thủ.
vi.R: Nhưng anh em được đốn những cây mà anh em biết là không có trái ăn được. Hãy dùng chúng để làm đường dốc và tháp để đánh thành đang chống lại anh em, cho đến khi thành ấy bị đánh bại.

ko.L: 다만 네가 알기에 먹을 [열매를 맺는] 나무가 아닌 나무는 없애고 베어서, 너와 전쟁을 하는 그 성읍이 함락될 때까지 그 성읍을 [치는] 공격 시설을 쌓아라.
ko.B: 다만 먹을 열매를 맺지 않는 줄 아는 나무만은 찍어 베어도 된다. 그것으로 너희와 싸우는 성읍이 함락될 때까지 그 성읍을 칠 공격 시설을 쌓아라.
ko.R: 그러나 먹을 열매를 맺지 않는 줄 아는 나무는 베어도 됩니다. 그 나무로 언덕과 망대를 쌓아, 여러분과 싸우는 성읍이 무너질 때까지 그 성읍을 공격하십시오.

decisions.choice: a tree for food: a tree that bears fruit people eat
decisions.reason: The rule turns on what a tree is for. Trees that do not bear food may be used for the war; those that feed people are spared (verse 19).

decisions.choice: siege works: ramps, walls and towers built against a city
decisions.reason: The word is the one for "siege" in verse 19. Here it means the works an army built from earth and timber to shut a city in and reach its walls (2 Kings 25:1; Ezekiel 4:2).

decisions.choice: until its going down: until it falls
decisions.reason: The verb means to go down. Used of a city it means its fall, as of high walls coming down in 28:52.

decisions.choice: ramps and towers to attack
decisions.reason: Readable describes the siege works instead of using the term (m2).

decisions.choice: may you destroy and cut down, to build siege works
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the building to the cutting, since the wood is cut for the siege works; the Hebrew joins them with "and".
